subject: Geography
description: Mountains, deserts, oceans, plateaus — world extremes & famous superlatives

questions.stem: The HIGHEST peak in the world is:
questions.explanation: Mount Everest — 8,848.86 m (newly measured 2020). K2 is second (8,611 m). Kangchenjunga is third (8,586 m) and the highest in India. Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) is Africa's highest. Everest is on Nepal-Tibet border.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The LARGEST desert in the world (by area) is:
questions.explanation: Antarctica is technically a polar desert (very low precipitation) covering ~14.2 million sq km — the largest desert. Sahara (~9.2 million sq km) is the largest HOT desert. Desert definition: <25 cm annual precipitation.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the OCEAN/SEA with its LOCATION-FACT. A. Pacific Ocean.  B. Atlantic Ocean.  C. Indian Ocean.  D. Arctic Ocean. List-II: 1. World's largest and deepest (Mariana Trench).  2. S-shaped; separates Americas from Europe/Africa.  3. Only ocean named after a country.  4. Smallest ocean, frozen most of the year.
questions.explanation: Pacific — largest (~165 million km²), deepest point = Challenger Deep in Mariana Trench (10,994 m). Atlantic — S-shape. Indian — only ocean named for a country. Arctic — smallest (~14 million km²), mostly frozen.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The IMAGINARY line at 0° longitude passing through Greenwich is called:
questions.explanation: Prime Meridian — 0° longitude, passes through Greenwich, London. Equator — 0° latitude (dividing N/S hemispheres). Tropic of Cancer — 23.5° N. International Date Line — approximately 180° longitude (zig-zags to avoid splitting countries).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: 'ROOF OF THE WORLD' is a term often used for:

options.option_text: Tibetan Plateau (sometimes also used for this)

questions.explanation: The Pamir Mountains ('Pamir Knot', intersection of Hindu Kush, Karakoram, Kunlun, Tian Shan, Himalayas) is traditionally called the 'Roof of the World'. The Tibetan Plateau is also often given this epithet — both are acceptable in Indian exam context; Pamir is the more classical answer.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which is the DEEPEST lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal (Siberia, Russia) — maximum depth 1,642 m, the deepest and one of the oldest (~25 million years). Caspian Sea is the LARGEST lake by area. Dead Sea — lowest elevation lake (~430 m below sea level).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The HIGHEST waterfall in the world is:
questions.explanation: Angel Falls (Salto Ángel), Venezuela — 979 m total drop — world's highest uninterrupted waterfall. Victoria Falls (Zambia/Zimbabwe) is widest+highest-flow. Niagara (USA/Canada) is most popular tourist. Iguazu (Brazil/Argentina) has the broadest spread.
